title: PostgreSQL Connection Pool Saturation & Automated Circuit Breaker Recovery

timeline.event_description: Batch client initiates 500 parallel document upload requests
PostgreSQL connection pool saturation reaches 92% (46/50 leases)
Runbook RB-DB-002 activated by automated Incident Decision Engine
Application circuit breaker opened to shed non-critical query load
Terminated 12 idle connections and reloaded PgBouncer pool
Health checks confirmed active connections reduced to 24/50; circuit breaker closed (MTTR=8.8s)
Postmortem generated and knowledge base resolution updated

impact_summary: 32 document upload requests experienced a transient 2-second queue delay; zero tasks dropped or failed.
root_cause_analysis: Unbounded burst client concurrency exceeded the configured PgBouncer default pool ceiling before database connection recycling could release idle connection handles.
remediation_steps_taken: Automated circuit breaker activated to throttle incoming write spikes
pg_terminate_backend executed on idle-in-transaction connection handles
PgBouncer pool multiplexer reloaded and connection health verified
preventive_action_items: Expand PgBouncer default pool size from 50 to 100 in infrastructure/k8s/postgres.yaml
Enforce SQLAlchemy connection pool timeout to 10 seconds with pre-ping validation
Deploy proactive queue rate limiter on /api/v1/documents/upload endpoint
